review_candidates.title: DSP Network Manager

Speedaf Logistics (Switzerland) Sarl. is building a two-tier distribution network here - a central sortation hub handling up to 50,000 parcels per day (4000 sqm), supported by regional sub-distribution centres (500 sqm sub-DCs) in Zurich, Bern, and Lausanne . Role Overview You will be responsible for identifying, recruiting, onboarding, and managing DSP partners across Switzerland to achieve full national last-mile delivery coverage. You will act as the primary relationship owner between Speedaf and its DSP network, ensuring operational standards, contractual compliance, and sustainable business growth for both parties. Over time, you will also support DSPs in developing local-to-local parcel volume to deepen network density. Key Responsibilities DSP Network Development Map delivery coverage gaps across all Swiss postal zones (PLZ areas) and build a structured DSP recruitment pipeline to achieve full national coverage Identify, evaluate, and onboard qualified DSP candidates, including existing courier operators, fleet owners, logistics SMEs, and independent delivery contractors Conduct capability assessments covering: fleet size, driver headcount, operational area, PostCom compliance status, insurance coverage, and system integration readiness Negotiate and execute DSP service agreements covering service area, SLA commitments, rate cards, KPI framework, and data protection obligations Maintain a DSP pipeline tracker and report weekly recruitment progress against coverage targets Market Intelligence Develop and maintain a detailed competitive landscape of Swiss last-mile delivery market players, and emerging courier networks Analyse competitors' DSP/franchise models, coverage maps, rate structures, parcel volume capacities, and technology platforms Identify underserved zones, capacity gaps, and partnership opportunities in the Swiss market Provide regular market intelligence reports to senior management to inform network strategy and pricing decisions DSP Performance & Relationship Management Serve as the primary point of contact for all DSP partners post-onboarding Conduct regular business reviews with DSPs covering volume trends, SLA performance, KPI compliance, billing accuracy, and operational issues Work with the operations team to support DSPs in improving delivery success rates, POD quality, tracking completeness, and return handling efficiency Identify and escalate underperforming DSPs; develop and execute corrective action plans or manage replacement recruitment where necessary Local Business Development Support Support DSPs in developing domestic Switzerland-to-Switzerland parcel volume by identifying local e-commerce merchants, retailers, and SME shippers as potential customers Collaborate with the sales team to create DSP-facing commercial materials, territory-specific pitch decks, and local market entry plans Provide DSPs with lead referrals, sales tools, and Speedaf product training to enable local business origination Requirements 3+ years of experience in last-mile logistics, express delivery, or courier network development in Switzerland or Western Europe Deep understanding of the Swiss domestic parcel market, including Swiss Post's network structure, DPD Switzerland's franchise/DSP model, and Planzer's regional coverage approach Proven track record of recruiting and managing delivery partners, franchise operators, or subcontractor networks Strong knowledge of Swiss PostCom registration requirements, cantonal business regulations, and labour law compliance for courier operations Experience in contract negotiation, commercial structuring, and partner onboarding Proficient in CRM tools, route planning software, and logistics management systems Fluent in English; German and/or French required; Chinese is a strong advantage Swiss driving licence (Category B); willingness to travel nationally What We Offer Competitive base salary with performance-linked bonus tied to network coverage and DSP volume KPIs Direct impact on building Speedaf's Swiss network from the ground up High-visibility role with career progression into regional or country leadership Exposure to a fast-scaling international logistics platform operating across Europe, Africa, and Asia

review_candidates.title: Software Engineer (Platform Security) x Mosaico
review_candidates.description: Location: Reggio Emilia - Remoto Reporting to: CTO Compensation (RAL): € 45.000–60.000 lordi/anno + stock options + welfare package Azienda Mosaico è una data platform open-source per la robotica e la physical AI. Stiamo risolvendo un problema infrastrutturale difficile: gli strumenti che esistono oggi per salvare, indicizzare e recuperare dati sensoriali ad alta frequenza sono troppo primitivi o troppo dolorosi da usare a scala. Stiamo costruendo il pezzo mancante, e lo facciamo in open: licenza Apache 2.0, roadmap pubblica, community vera — teniamo a una codebase che la gente voglia leggere e a cui voglia contribuire, non solo usare. Siamo basati a Reggio Emilia, lavoriamo con team in ambito difesa, automotive e agritech, e stiamo costruendo un'offerta commerciale sopra il core open-source. Cosa farai Entrerai in un team piccolo e focalizzato per progettare e costruire da zero il modulo di security di Mosaico — auth, authorization e gRPC sicuro, in Go — come founding member sul prodotto. C'è molto lavoro di design prima ancora della prima riga di codice in produzione: threat modeling, design della superficie API, semantica dei permessi, ciclo di vita dei token e pattern di integrazione con il resto della piattaforma. Se ti piace ragionare a fondo su un problema prima di risolverlo, è quel tipo di ruolo. Il modulo si integra direttamente con mosaicod via gRPC, quindi lavorerai con Protocol Buffers, service definition e le specifiche del mettere in sicurezza la comunicazione gRPC in un ambiente ad alto throughput, a stretto contatto con il team che costruisce il core in Rust. Nel concreto: Co-progetterai l'architettura del nuovo modulo insieme al resto del team, dal threat model ai contratti API Implementerai un servizio Go che si integra con mosaicod via gRPC e viene consumato dai client SDK Progetterai pattern di comunicazione gRPC sicuri: channel security, interceptor, propagazione dell'auth via metadata Definirai e documenterai le primitive di security: flussi di autenticazione, modelli di autorizzazione, gestione dei token, ciclo di vita delle chiavi Contribuirai alle code review e aiuterai a definire gli standard di ingegneria del modulo Lavorerai su uno stack poliglotta (Go, Rust, Python), interfacciandoti con componenti interni della piattaforma e integrazioni esterne Stack — Must have Solida esperienza in Go, inclusi servizi in produzione e pattern idiomatici Basi robuste di information security: protocolli di autenticazione (OAuth2, OIDC, JWT), modelli di autorizzazione (RBAC, ABAC), primitive crittografiche, secure API design e le superfici d'attacco più comuni Esperienza hands-on con gRPC e Protocol Buffers, incluso il design dei servizi e la messa in sicurezza di endpoint gRPC in produzione Capacità di contribuire al system design, non solo all'implementazione: a tuo agio a fare whiteboarding sui modelli di permessi e a discutere i tradeoff Esperienza nel costruire o gestire servizi security-sensitive Autonomia e rigore: è un team piccolo, l'ownership conta Inglese fluente, scritto e parlato Nice to have Esperienza con Rust o voglia vera di impararlo Background in sistemi distribuiti o data infrastructure Familiarità con secrets management, PKI o primitive di hardware security Esperienza con Apache Arrow (su cui poggia il gRPC nel nostro stack) Contributi open-source Annuncio aperto a candidati di ogni genere (L. 903/77 e 125/91), età e nazionalità (D.Lgs. 215/03 e 216/03).
